h1: No-Code Waitlist — AI & SaaS Call to Action Design
tagline: “A new way to think and create with computers” — the whole call-to-action block is composed around that line, down to the animation timings.
summary: Call to action reference for an AI or SaaS product — looping video, React and Tailwind CSS, #020004 base and #7C78C7 accent.
about: No-Code Waitlist is the call-to-action block reference for an AI or SaaS product, and the brief behind it is a full build spec rather than a mood board. The page's own headline reads “A new way to think and create with computers”, and the composition is built around those exact words. The palette is deep indigo #020004 underneath, tint #FFFFFF for the type and muted blue #7C78C7 carrying the accents, set in Inter. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 988x720 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. The page keeps its motion to 60ms transitions and a looping video bed. Take it on when the call-to-action block needs a decided order before any new sections are added.

layout.title: Links before the action
layout.body: The bar is the quietest part of the composition: wordmark, a short row of links and one #7C78C7 action, all held at the smallest type step in the brief. The links are set below the wordmark in size, and the #7C78C7 action is the only element in the bar with any weight.

layout.title: Nothing here is inherited
layout.body: Nothing here is eyeballed. The spec fixes type from 13px to 64px, 100vh sections, 14px spacing steps and 60ms transitions, and the rest of the layout derives from those values. Each value maps to one job: a type step, a gap, a radius or a transition. Measure before you adjust.

layout.title: Full-frame video, no panel
layout.body: The media is one 9.4s clip cropped to cover the 988x720 frame, so it never letterboxes at any width. The loop is short enough (9.4s) that the eye reads it as texture rather than as a timeline.

layout.title: One row, no drawers
layout.body: The bar sits over the 988x720 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

motion.title: A loop, not a timeline
motion.body: Ambient movement comes from the 9.4s 988x720 loop rather than from scroll effects, which keeps the page calm and the type readable. The loop is cropped to cover, which means the composition does not depend on a particular frame size.

motion.title: One element arrives
motion.body: A typewriter pass is the only entrance on the page, so there is one motion idea to maintain. Timing is derived from one value, so a longer line takes longer without being hand-tuned. Do not add a second entrance.

style.glass: Panels are translucent over deep indigo #020004, and the type on top stays at full contrast so the effect never costs readability.
notes: Media is specified at 988x720 and a 9.4s loop, so a replacement should match the crop and the loop length.
The display line is Inter at the top of a 13–64px scale, with the interface text on the same face.
Font roles are assigned rather than mixed here, and 13–64px is the range the whole scale works in.

customize: Hold the 988x720 frame when you swap the content; the composition was solved against that ratio and a wider export pushes the type off.
Change the copy first, then the accent, then the media: the 988x720 frame was solved in that order and reversing it costs a re-layout.
Replace the video with a still at 988x720 if the 9.4s loop is too heavy for the page you are shipping.
Replace the copy in the Inter stack first, then re-check the #7C78C7 accent against the media behind it.

editorial.title: How No-Code Waitlist sequences the first read
editorial.body: Committing to one reading path means other paths are closed. The brief accepts that, fixes navigation, the headline, the announcement badge, the stats row and the form in place, and spends type from 13px to 64px and 100vh sections on making the route obvious. A SaaS reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: What an AI or SaaS product gains here
editorial.body: When you brief a SaaS call-to-action block, the hard part is deciding what the first screen refuses to say. No-Code Waitlist answers that in advance: one display line, navigation, the headline, the announcement badge, the stats row and the form behind it. No-Code Waitlist states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

editorial.title: What to change first in No-Code Waitlist
editorial.body: You do not need to rebuild the call-to-action block to make it yours. Replace the headline and the media, keep the scale (type from 13px to 64px and 100vh sections), and the layout still reads as designed. The composition is the reusable part, and it survives a different brand.

steps: Stage the prompt in Studio and read it once against the 988x720 capture before you generate.
Drop your product name in, then replace #7C78C7 with your own accent and re-check the contrast.
Set the brand first: product name, the #7C78C7 accent and a headline that replaces the reference's.
Type the product name and the #7C78C7 accent before you touch the layout.
Set your brand first: product name, the #7C78C7 accent and the headline that replaces the reference's.

faq.question: What can I do with the No-Code Waitlist brief once I have it?
faq.answer: Everything quoted on the page comes from the captured 6,532-character brief rather than from a description written afterwards. That is why the numbers and the prose agree.

faq.question: What does the brief behind No-Code Waitlist actually contain?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 988x720, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: Do I need React and Tailwind CSS to rebuild No-Code Waitlist?
faq.answer: No-Code Waitlist was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

audience: Start from type from 13px to 64px and 100vh sections and let the palette follow, because the spacing is what makes this call-to-action block read.
